summary: SFTPConnection is a decorator connection that opens a paramiko SFTPClient channel over an SSHConnection it exclusively owns. connect() reuses a healthy SSH connection, replaces any existing channel, and on failure releases both the channel and SSH; disconnect() closes the channel then the SSH connection, attaching secondary failures as notes.
key_classes: SFTPConnection — decorator over SSHConnection exposing paramiko.SFTPClient as .client
key_functions: SFTPConnection.connect() -> Self — connect SSH if needed, then open_sftp()
SFTPConnection.disconnect() -> None — close channel, then SSH, preserving the primary error
extension_points: Accepts any object with is_connected/connect/disconnect/client.open_sftp(), typed as t.Any
lifecycle_notes: Owns its SSHConnection: disconnect() always tears down SSH; reconnect reuses healthy SSH and only replaces the channel.
Failed startup releases both channel and SSH; cleanup failures become notes on the primary exception.
__enter__ returns self without connecting; __exit__ disconnects and attaches cleanup failures as notes when the body raised.
is_connected reflects only the SFTP channel, not SSH health.
documentation_hooks: SFTP connections: ownership of the SSH layer and reconnect semantics
Connection lifetime section of README (SFTP exclusive ownership)
risks: ssh_connection is typed t.Any, so the type checker cannot catch passing a non-SSH connection.
Closing the SFTP channel does not close channels opened by other callers on the same SSHClient, but disconnect() closes the whole SSH client, which would break any shared use.

evidence.detail: Docstring: owns the inner SSHConnection exclusively; disconnect tears down both
create_connection returns SFTPConnection(SSHConnection(...)) for SFTP provider
Connection lifetime: SFTP exclusively owns its SSH connection; successful channel replacement reuses healthy SSH
